title: A Lunch Box Ready to Go
subtheme: A Lunch Box Ready to Go
description: Pack familiar foods and a drink into a carry-along lunch box.
cardDescription: Pack familiar foods and a drink into a carry-along lunch box.
focus: The setting is a Lunch Box Ready to Go. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Container with a base and sides
Part held when carrying or using something
Food made with filling between pieces of bread
Sweet produce such as an apple
Cloth or paper square used at a meal
Utensil with a small bowl at one end
Round tree fruit with a core
Put items into a bag or box

answerNotes.BOX: A box is a container rather than its contents. In a hobby clue, a kit may come in a box but the two words are not interchangeable.
answerNotes.LID: A lid is a removable cover. On a cooking pot it helps contain heat and steam; on a jar it closes the opening.
answerNotes.HANDLE: A handle is the part made for the hand to grip. Its shape depends on whether the object is carried, pulled, poured, or turned.
answerNotes.SANDWICH: A sandwich places a filling between pieces of bread. An open-faced version uses just one supporting slice.
answerNotes.FRUIT: Everyday fruit dishes can mix several kinds of plant produce. The serving word is culinary and does not require a botanical classification.
answerNotes.SPOON: A spoon has a small bowl at one end. It can hold liquid, unlike the prongs of a fork.
answerNotes.APPLE: An apple has a peel, flesh, and a seed-bearing core. Cider is made by pressing apples for their juice.
answerNotes.BAG: A bag is a flexible carrying container. A pocket is generally a smaller compartment attached to clothing or another bag.

words: Cold storage compartment keeping ice cream frozen
Day and month on a calendar

answerNotes.LABEL: A label identifies an item or its contents. It can carry a name, date, size, or address depending on the scene.
answerNotes.DATE: A date identifies a day, usually with a month and year. It can distinguish a photo's occasion from the day its note was written.
answerNotes.LID: A lid is a removable cover. On a cooking pot it helps contain heat and steam; on a jar it closes the opening.
answerNotes.BOX: A box is a container rather than its contents. In a hobby clue, a kit may come in a box but the two words are not interchangeable.
answerNotes.BAG: A bag is a flexible carrying container. A pocket is generally a smaller compartment attached to clothing or another bag.
answerNotes.ICE: Ice is solid water. It absorbs heat as it melts, which helps cool a drink.
answerNotes.SHELF: A shelf is a horizontal storage surface. A drawer is a compartment that slides in and out.

words: Short everyday name for the appliance holding chilled food
Oval food with a shell, white, and yolk
Pull-out compartment in a piece of furniture
Movable panel at a room's entrance
Dairy food sold in blocks or slices

answerNotes.SHELF: A shelf is a horizontal storage surface. A drawer is a compartment that slides in and out.
answerNotes.MILK: Milk is a dairy liquid used in drinks and batters. Cream is the richer portion, with a higher fat content.
answerNotes.EGG: A hen's egg has a shell, white, and yolk. Recipes sometimes use only one inner part rather than the whole egg.
answerNotes.DRAWER: A drawer slides in and out of furniture. Its front may have a handle, while dividers separate the contents inside.
answerNotes.DOOR: A door is the movable panel at an entrance. Hinges let it swing, while a latch or lock holds it closed.
answerNotes.BUTTER: Butter is made by churning cream. It adds flavor and fat to baked goods as well as serving as a spread.
answerNotes.CHEESE: Cheese comes in many textures and flavors. Sharp describes flavor, while a wedge describes the shape of a cut portion.
answerNotes.JAR: A jar has a wide opening that makes spooning and filling easier. A bottle usually has a narrower neck.

answerNotes.PLATE: A plate is flatter than a bowl. Its broad surface is useful for separate portions of a meal.
answerNotes.SLICE: A slice is a flat cut portion of food. Slice can also be the action of cutting food into those portions.
answerNotes.KNIFE: A knife cuts with a blade. In the kitchen, the board beneath the food supports the ingredient while it is sliced.
answerNotes.GLASS: Glass is usually transparent but can also be colored. A glass is a drinking vessel, while glass without an article can name the material.
answerNotes.SWEET: Sweet describes flavor, not temperature or texture. A food can be sweet and cold, or sweet and warm.

answerNotes.BREAD: Bread may be a whole loaf or pieces cut from it. A loaf is counted as a whole, while a slice is one flat portion.
answerNotes.BOX: A box is a container rather than its contents. In a hobby clue, a kit may come in a box but the two words are not interchangeable.
answerNotes.CRUST: Crust can mean a pie's pastry shell or a loaf's baked outer surface. Both are outer parts, but they are made differently.
answerNotes.SLICE: A slice is a flat cut portion of food. Slice can also be the action of cutting food into those portions.
answerNotes.LID: A lid is a removable cover. On a cooking pot it helps contain heat and steam; on a jar it closes the opening.
answerNotes.WOOD: Wood comes from trees and has a grain. Following that grain when sanding usually leaves a smoother surface.
answerNotes.COUNTER: A counter is a raised work or serving surface. In a shop it separates the customer area from the worker's space.
answerNotes.KNIFE: A knife cuts with a blade. In the kitchen, the board beneath the food supports the ingredient while it is sliced.
answerNotes.BAG: A bag is a flexible carrying container. A pocket is generally a smaller compartment attached to clothing or another bag.
